topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, reviews previous practical work, and outlines the learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and experimental cell transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the historical study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established assays for testing oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Cancer gene classifications and functional mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the classes of cancer genes and examine how mutations affect regulatory pathways through differences in gene dosage and dominant-negative mechanisms.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability and detail the specific DNA repair failures and mitotic errors that cause them.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of mutations drives tumor evolution in both sporadic multi-step models and inherited cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Closing remarks and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by offering to answer questions, recommending supplementary reading, and previewing the next topic.
